answer: According to arXiv 2503.18979, the probability of α exceeding αc is effectively equivalent to bounding the tail probability of Y for large values of y. Specifically, if near αc the jump in x scales like (α - αc)p for some p > 0, then bounding Pr(Y > y) for large y is essentially the same as bounding Pr(α > αc). The function η(y) plays a crucial role in this relationship; it is a function that is non-negative and approaches zero as y approaches infinity. This means that for sufficiently large y, the small offset introduced by η(y) becomes negligible, allowing the two probabilities to be closely related. Thus, as y becomes large, the behavior of the tail distribution of Y aligns with the behavior of the probability that α exceeds the critical threshold αc.
